⇧⌘O flattens the selected root once in the background — the one feature that walks a whole tree — keyed by root tree id, cancellable, capped at 200 000 entries, and offers fuzzy jump-to-file. Every directory read lands in the shared tree cache. In the working tree it walks disk instead (
), once per opening of the panel, so gitignored files such as
are found; ignored folders the tree does not track are skipped unread.
The sidebar's "Working Tree" row shows files on disk with a status overlay against

The tree filters rows it already read, so the toggle reads nothing; path search and the change list, which leaves out untracked hidden files so they never ride along in a commit, follow the same setting.

Files and Changes show a banner at the top of the sidebar in place of the ref list, so the tree and the change list get its height. In Files it names what the tree browses (the working tree and its branch, a commit, or a ref) and opens the ref list in a popover under it on a click or ⌘B; arrows move, Return picks, Escape or a click outside closes. In History, ⌘B focuses the sidebar's ref filter instead. In Changes it names the checked-out branch and is read-only, since the change list always compares the working tree with

A lane column in the History pane draws the topology of the paged commits:
(RcGitKit, pure, tested) assigns lanes strictly sequentially from

, so appending a page never reshuffles drawn rows, and the builder is cached per tip alongside the pages. Rendering clamps at 12 drawn lanes; the column hides while a path scope or search shows a filtered list. No core or FFI change.

A filter bar over the History pane (⇧⌘F) matches message or author as the user types, with optional date bounds; matches stream in scan chunks with a progress count, and a hex query jumps straight to that revision. Search pages through the same resumable walk as path history,

commits per page; a since-bound uses gix's commit-time cutoff so the walk terminates at the window instead of scanning to the root. Under a path scope the search applies the path history's path-change test too. No index is ever built. The CLI gained

In Files, ⇧⌘F opens a panel that finds a literal string in every file below the browsed root: blobs, or the files on disk while browsing the working tree. Smart case: a query with no uppercase letter ignores ASCII case. Return searches; hits land per batch, grouped by file with each line's excerpt, and Return on a line opens the file in source mode with the match selected. It reads the path-search file list, so nothing new walks the tree, then asks the core for one batch at a time (

), each capped at 8 MiB read and cancellable between batches. A blob shared by several paths is read once; files over 1 MiB and binary files are skipped, and the search stops at 2,000 matching lines. No index is built. The CLI gained

"Show File History" on tree rows and ⌥⌘Y for the open file scope the History pane to the commits that changed one path, with a chip to clear. A history walk filtered by path compares the entry at the path against every parent (clean merges hide, root commits count, renames are not followed), examining at most
commits per page, each page resuming where the last stopped, so pages stream in chunks and a scope change between chunks cancels the rest. Pages cache by

alongside the tree diff: full message body, committer when it differs from the author, refs pointing at the commit (computed from the ref listing, no extra walk), and parent links. Parent links and revision jumps go through

Every repository opens in its own tab of one native window group (⌘T for an empty tab, "+" in the tab bar, ⇧⌘[ / ⇧⌘] to move between them). Each tab is a full

— model, caches, and watchers stay alive while the tab is in the background — so switching tabs reorders windows and reads nothing. Opening a repository that is already open selects its existing tab. ⌘W closes the tab on screen, ⇧⌘W the whole window group.
(RcGitKit) persists the tab list and selection through

— recorded on every open, close, and at quit — and a relaunch reopens them. ⌘W drops the tab's repository from that list; ⇧⌘W and ⌘Q keep theirs, so the next launch comes back with them. The restore also drops the repositories that no longer open.

⌘[ and ⌘], the toolbar arrows, a two-finger swipe, and a mouse's fourth and fifth buttons step through the places you went: files opened, commits picked, History scoped to a path, the Files/History/Changes pane, the ref browsed, and the tab in front. One list covers every tab, so a step back from one repository can land in another.
names where a tab is and

returns to one, redoing only what differs. A stop names what it showed and reads it again on return: a ref that moved shows its new tip, a file that is gone leaves the pane empty. The list lives in memory, keeps 200 stops, and drops a tab's stops when the tab closes. The commit detail's back arrow is the same step, shown while it lands on another commit. No core or FFI change.
